blocks.text: What account executives do in Zoom on Mac

Most account executives use Zoom on Mac for three jobs. You host discovery calls and demos. You send booking links so prospects can pick a time. You review what happened on the call, with an AI summary or with call analytics if your company pays for them. The Zoom desktop app handles all three. Each job depends on a license or an admin setting, so check those before you plan a week around a feature.

Time is the reason small Zoom habits matter. Salesforce's fifth State of Sales report, published in December 2022 from 7,775 responses, found that sales reps spend just 28% of their week selling. Most of the week is not spent selling. A summary you do not write by hand, or a booking link you do not type out, gives time back for the next call. Some newer percentages circulate online without a Salesforce source. Quote the 28% figure with its date and survey size, and check Salesforce's own pages before you repeat any other number.
How to schedule a Zoom meeting on Mac

Scheduling is the first thing you do in Zoom most days. Zoom's support article gives the macOS path. Start in the navigation bar and click Home. If you do not see Home, click More, then Home. Click Schedule, then enter a topic and a time. Add invitees if you want them on the invite. Open Settings only if you need to change meeting options. Then click Save.

items: Click Home in the navigation bar. If Home is missing, click More, then Home.
Click Schedule.
Type a topic the prospect will recognize, such as their problem, not your product name.
Enter a start time.
Add invitees, or skip this step and share the link yourself.
Open Settings only if you need to change meeting options.
Click Save.
If calendar integration is on, choose Back to editing, Don't send, or Send.

blocks.text: That last choice matters. Back to editing keeps the meeting open so you can change it. Don't send saves the meeting without emailing anyone. Send emails the invite right away. Choose Don't send when you want to check the time and topic first, especially for a prospect you have not met.

blocks.title: Home is hidden?
blocks.text: On a narrow window, Home can sit under More. Widen the window, or click More first. Then look for Schedule inside Home. Ask Lazur to point at Home if you cannot find it during a call.
Zoom Scheduler booking links for prospects

Scheduler is the booking page you send to a prospect. In the Zoom desktop app, open it from the More menu in the navigation bar. Zoom's Scheduler guide lists the steps for Windows, macOS, and Linux together. The Mac menu names may not match the guide word for word. Look for the function, not the exact label.

Scheduler is not free. It needs a paid Scheduler Basic or Scheduler license. Your admin must enable it. Your desktop app must meet the supported version. You also need one connected calendar, either Google Calendar, Microsoft 365, or Zoom Calendar. Only one calendar service works at a time, so pick the calendar that shows your real availability.

items: Confirm your admin enabled Scheduler and gave you a Scheduler license.
Check that your desktop app meets the version Zoom lists for Scheduler.
Connect the calendar that shows your true free and busy time.
Open the link in a private browser window and check the slots it shows.
Remember that you can connect only one calendar service at a time.

blocks.title: Shared steps, not Mac steps
blocks.text: Zoom's Scheduler guide has no Mac-only steps. It covers Windows, macOS, and Linux together. If a label on your screen differs from the guide, match the function and move on. Do not spend a live call hunting for an exact label.
Meeting summary templates: pick one and know what it does

A meeting summary template shapes the AI summary Zoom writes after a call. Your admin creates and customizes templates in AI Studio. Your admin also decides which templates you can access. The support article describes admin setup, not building templates as an end user. Plan on choosing from the list you get.

To pick a template in the Zoom desktop app, find the Zoom AI section in the meeting settings. Open the Meeting summary template dropdown and choose one. If you skip this step, the admin's default template applies. Check the choice before any call that matters, because the default may not fit that call.

The support article names the dropdown but does not walk through every menu step on the Mac. If you cannot find it, ask Lazur where it is. Lazur circles the control and labels it. You still pick the template yourself.

blocks.text: The 32,000 character limit matters on long calls. A long discovery call can produce a long summary that is hard to scan. Read the summary once against your own notes. Then trust the parts you checked and fix the rest.

blocks.text: Zoom Revenue Accelerator: what you need before you turn it on

Zoom Revenue Accelerator analyzes recorded sales meetings. It needs more setup than Scheduler or summaries. Your account must be Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Zoom Phone standalone. Your user needs a Revenue Accelerator license in the Essentials, Premium, or Elite tier. Your calendar must be Zoom-integrated. Cloud recording and audio transcription must be on.

The desktop app must be version 5.12.6 or higher on macOS. An admin assigns the license. If you do not see the feature, you probably do not have a license yet. Ask your admin rather than digging through settings.

The biggest limit is simple. Revenue Accelerator only analyzes recorded meetings. No recording means no analysis. Recording consent must come from external participants. Recordings that a retention policy deletes also disappear from Revenue Accelerator. Plan for that before a quarter-end review.

blocks.title: Consent comes first
blocks.text: Ask external participants for consent before you hit record. Do not record a prospect who has not agreed. Zoom's support article makes consent a requirement, so treat it as a hard rule.

Once it is set up, the Deals page can pull CRM deal and opportunity information, such as deal size and activity time. Sales Supervisors, or users with Scorecard Management permission, create and manage scorecards. If you lack that permission, ask your supervisor which scorecards apply to your calls.
Edge cases that catch account executives

Some problems look like bugs but are settings. A missing Schedule button can mean Home is hidden. A missing summary template can mean your admin has not enabled templates. A missing Revenue Accelerator screen can mean no license. Work through these checks in order before you contact support.

Features like summary templates depend on your account type. Check the account type first when a feature is missing. If your company has more than one Zoom account, make sure you are signed in to the one with the license.

items: Open the Zoom desktop app and confirm your version meets the minimums in the table above.
Click Home. If Home is missing, click More, then Home.
Ask your admin whether Scheduler, summary templates, and Revenue Accelerator are enabled for you.
Connect your calendar once and confirm the invite prompt works with a test meeting you host.
Write down which summary template your admin set as the default.

blocks.text: Mistakes account executives make in Zoom on Mac

items: Assuming Scheduler works with any calendar. It takes one connected calendar service at a time.
Expecting Revenue Accelerator to analyze a call you did not record.
Treating the Scheduler guide as Mac-only. It covers Windows, macOS, and Linux together.
Quoting a selling-time figure from a blog without checking Salesforce's own page.
Sending a booking link you never opened in a private window.
Accepting the default summary template without checking that it fits the call.
Recording a prospect before asking for consent.

blocks.text: Most of these come from skipping a short check. Do the setup check once, then recheck after a big update. A menu can move after an update, so look again when a feature seems to disappear.
Where Lazur fits during a Zoom call

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons for you. It does not operate Zoom or any other app. It is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom, and it has no partnership with Zoom. Think of it as a second set of eyes that keeps your hands on the mouse.

Lazur is most useful in three moments. The first is when a menu has moved. The second is when you need a fast explanation of a screen during a call. The third is after the call, when you need a follow-up draft. Ask Lazur to write it, then paste it yourself.

Hold fn to dictate. Dictation writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Use it right after a call to capture the points you need while they are fresh. Snippets and a personal dictionary help with prospect names and product terms.
Keyboard shortcuts and Mac habits for calls

Shortcuts matter when a prospect is talking and you need a window, not a menu. Zoom lists its own call shortcuts on its support pages. The keys can change by version, so check that list before you memorize them. The Mac habits below work in most apps.

items: ⌘Tab switches between Zoom and your CRM or notes app without leaving the call.
⌃⌘F toggles full screen in many Mac apps, which helps when you share one window.
⌘Space opens Spotlight so you can find a file, contact, or PDF before the call.
⌘Q quits an app. Do not use it on Zoom in the middle of a meeting.
Hold ⌥⌘ to ask Lazur about the screen. Hold fn to dictate into any app.

blocks.text: A worked example: from booking to follow-up

Say a prospect asks for a call next week. Open Zoom, click Home, then Schedule. Type a topic in the prospect's words, such as their problem. Add the prospect as an invitee. Click Save. If the calendar prompt appears, choose Send to email the invite now.

Before the call, open the meeting settings and check the summary template. If your admin made a discovery template, pick it. If you cannot find the dropdown, ask Lazur to circle it. Then start the call with the screen you need already open.

After the call, read the summary against your notes. Hold fn and dictate a short follow-up with the three points that matter. Then ask Lazur to draft the email. Paste it into your mail app and send it yourself. Lazur drafts. You send.

If the prospect is worth a second meeting, send a Scheduler link for the next step. Open the link in a private window first. That check takes a minute and catches a broken slot before the prospect sees it.
Privacy, platform, and trial details before you rely on Lazur

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Still, check your company's policy on AI tools before you use any assistant with customer data.

Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. The free trial starts when you first open the app, and it needs no credit card. Plans, prices, and AI action limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing). Get the app from the [download page](/download).

faq.question: Is there a separate Zoom app for account executives on Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom's support pages describe one desktop app for macOS. What changes is your account type, your admin settings, and the licenses assigned to you. Summary templates, Scheduler, and Revenue Accelerator each depend on those three things.

faq.question: Why don't I see Schedule or Home in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: On a narrow window, Home can sit under More. Click More, then Home, and look for Schedule. If Home is still missing, check your account type with your admin.

faq.question: Do I need a paid license for Zoom Scheduler?
faq.answer: Yes. Scheduler needs a paid Scheduler Basic or Scheduler license, Scheduler enabled, a supported desktop app version, and one connected calendar. Google Calendar, Microsoft 365, or Zoom Calendar all work, but only one service at a time.

faq.question: Why can't I choose a meeting summary template?
faq.answer: Your admin has to enable meeting summary templates and decide which ones you can access. You need a Business, Business Plus, Enterprise, or Education account and desktop app 6.4.0 or higher on macOS. If no template is picked, the admin default applies.

faq.question: Can Revenue Accelerator analyze a call I did not record?
faq.answer: No. Revenue Accelerator only analyzes recorded meetings. Recording consent must come from external participants, and recordings deleted under a retention policy are removed from it too.

faq.question: Does Lazur join my Zoom call or click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Zoom for you. It answers out loud, points at things, and guides you one click at a time. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Does Lazur plug into Zoom?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom, and it has no partnership with Zoom. It works alongside the app as a voice assistant on your Mac.

faq.question: Which Macs does Lazur run on?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, with Apple silicon and Intel Macs supported. Windows is planned but not available yet.

faq.question: Where do I check the current Zoom version for Mac?
faq.answer: Use Zoom's release notes for macOS. Zoom now puts the Zoom Workplace app release notes for all platforms in one article. Compare your version with the minimums on this page, and ask your admin if you are unsure.
